newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Bund, BTP vols mired ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Bund, BTP vols mired ahead of data.

text.p: Bund and BTP options' volatility was supported by the prospect of key U.S. economic data, despite limited trade, traders said on Tuesday.
Traders said there was relatively little excitement in the underlying futures and options contracts, and open interest showed that many investors have only limited exposure.

"Volatilities are holding firm, and although things are quite quiet, no-one is happy selling vol," said a broker at a major British brokerage on the LIFFE floor. "There are lots of figures and it's too uncertain."
The first quarter employment cost index, and U.S. March durable goods data are scheduled for release at 1230 GMT, while April consumer confidence is due at 1400 GMT.
On Friday, the April non-farm payroll report is on the agenda -- and traders said there was little chance of major movement before that was out of the way.
Implied volatility of June Bund options on June Bund futures was at 5.70 percent, up 0.10 from Monday. July and August serial options were up slightly at 5.65 percent.
June Bund futures were up 0.10 at 100.51 by 1145 GMT.
A trader at a French brokerage said straddles were actively traded, with the 100.50 through 102.00 strikes seeing most trade in calls, and 99.50 through 100.50 strikes on the put side.
The British brokerage trader said volumes in BTPs were very low, with only small lots going through.
June options volatility was unchanged at 8.40 percent.
The underlying June BTP future was at 126.51, down 19 basis points on the day.
